notes: The doubled netunim netunim is split rather than fused, since the ASV spends a separate English word on the emphasis: the first takes wholly and the second the predicate are given (compare rule 56). Assigning wholly to the second occurrence was the competing reading.
even is added under rule 16: the appositive bekor kol carries no marker, and the clause's markers stand elsewhere, which rule 16 forbids reaching across.
The of before all belongs to kol as the rectum of bekor (rule 19) — it stands before all, not before children — leaving min unrepresented under rule 40.
bekor heads on born as a tie under rule 31; heading on first was available, and the chapter is consistent here with NUM.8.17 and NUM.8.18.
